title: Look up integer sequences in the OEIS
when: recognizing the numbers that a computation or a statement produced: the numbers where a statement holds, the first values of a count
finding the name, the offset and the next terms of a sequence you have the terms or the number of
whenNot: proving anything: a match is a lookup and gives a form to conjecture, which only a Lean proof settles
fewer than six terms, or terms that are mostly equal: too many sequences match, and a match says little
a table of numbers: read it by rows, by columns or by antidiagonals, and look up each reading

terms.description: Consecutive terms of the sequence, in order. A number past 2^53 is given as decimal text

id.description: The number of a sequence, such as A000045, instead of terms

count.description: How many sequences the site says match; results holds the first page of them

offset.description: The index of the first term

terms.description: The terms the site shows, as decimal text

examples.title: a sequence recognized from its first terms

results.name: Fibonacci numbers: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1.

examples.note: The count and the page are the site's; this one is shortened.

results.name: Fibonacci numbers: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1.

implementations.description: The OEIS's JSON search (/search?q=...&fmt=json) through the client of @seshat/models, one request at a time with a pause between two. The address and the pauses are settings of the host profile. Not run against the site: it is not reachable from the development environment.

environment.site: oeis.org, or the address OEIS_URL gives (a mirror)
